newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sub-continent gold prices in a spin.
newsitem.headline: Indian sub-continent gold prices in a spin.

text.p: Gold prices, moving in the shadow of depressed world markets, are expected to fall further in the Indian sub-continent, dealers said on Monday.
A plunge in world gold prices to below $325 per ounce on Friday, their lowest in 12 years, triggered selling among traders in both India and Pakistan, dealers said.
The crash in world prices followed news that Australia's central bank had sold bullion from its reserves.
In Dubai, the feeder market for Indian sub-continent demand for gold, jewellery and bullion sales improved, dealers said, adding that the main re-export trade remained sluggish.
On the Bombay bullion market, standard gold fell 200 rupees per 10 grammes to 4,350 rupees in the week to Monday.
"There was some panic selling in the Indian market," said Babubhai Jain, a leading bullion dealer.
Jain said India's liberal import policy linked local bullion trade to world markets.
"Indian prices mirror the world trend at any given point of time," he said.
"Market sentiment is bearish and looking at the week's world prices as well as sluggish physical demand, I am expecting gold prices to fall further in the coming days," Jain said.
"In India, the wedding season is over and whatever money is left is now being shifted from gold to booming Indian stock markets," he said.
In Pakistan's main commercial city of Karachi, gold prices are likely to plunge further on low demand and in line with the depressed international trend, dealers said.
Gold prices hit a new-year low of 4,398 rupees per 10 grammes on Saturday from 4,415 on Friday.
"Gold rates will ease further this week," dealer Farooq Querashi said.
On the Karachi bullion market, the gold price fell 162 rupees to 4,398 rupees per 10 grammes.
Purchases of gold jewellery and bullion pieces, mainly by Dubai's large Indian and Pakistani expatriate community, had risen after several weeks of subdued activity.

"The price drop has been good for business. Lower prices have attracted people back into the market," said a wholesaler, anticipating that the upturn in demand would prompt higher imports into Dubai from suppliers Switzerland and Britain.
"People have flocked to the market in the last two days...Buying is more of a tradition that an investment decision. Dowries and family gifts still have to be bought," said one dealer.
Despite buoyant retail turnover prompted by "bargain- buying", Dubai's main trade in re-exporting gold to India was flat with little sign that India was increasing direct imports.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMMES in U.S. DOLLARS
(Conversion $1=35.78 Indian rupees, 40.56 Pakistani rupees and 3.67 UAE Dirhams) *Bombay prices July 7/June 30, Karachi July 5/June 28 and Dubai July 6/June 29.
